verdicts.reviewer_notes: Re-fetched https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/09/inaugurating-the-era-of-super-intelligence/ (several times, 2026-10-07). The page is headed 'Executive Order 14434' and its date line reads 'September 29, 2026', which matches event_date 2026-09-29. Sec. 2(a) reads: 'To the maximum extent permitted by law, executive departments and agencies (agencies) shall use "Super Intelligence" and "SI" in place of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" in official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports, policy documents, and other non-statutory documents within the executive branch.' The summary's list matches this. Sec. 2(b) (no required alteration of previously issued regulations, Presidential actions, contracts, grants or other historical documents) matches. Sec. 3(a) defines the terms by reference to 15 U.S.C. 9401(3), which matches. Sec. 3(b): within 60 days the APST, 'in consultation with the heads of other agencies as the APST deems appropriate, shall submit to the President proposed legislative language to establish a Federal definition'. The proposal shall include (i) an assessment of whether, and to what extent, the definition should 'modify, expand upon, or otherwise supersede' the existing statutory definition; (ii) 'any proposed conforming amendments, as appropriate, to existing statutory references to "artificial intelligence" and "AI"'; and (iii) recommendations for additional Presidential or executive action. The summary says the language goes 'to the President', which is correct. Its trailing 'as appropriate' directly follows the conforming-amendments clause, which is where the order puts it. The summary does not move the APST's 'deems appropriate' consultation qualifier. Minor non-misleading abbreviations: 'modify or supersede' omits 'expand upon' and 'to what extent', and clause (iii) is not mentioned. Because the summary uses 'including', these omissions are not misstatements. A second fetch found neither 'preemption' nor 'State law' on the page, so 'does not address preemption of state law' is supported by the text's silence. Sec. 4 contains the standard no-enforceable-rights clause, which supports 'no obligations for private parties on its face'. The stage in_force fits a signed EO with no delayed effective date. The White House is the issuing body, so the source is primary, and high confidence is justified because the full text was read. Grep of content/items and content/instruments found no 14434 or Super Intelligence entry. The tone is neutral.

Read the signed PDF in full: https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/FINAL-N-9-26-AI-EO-9.18.26-SIGNED.pdf. Verified: it is issued 'to become effective immediately' and signed 'this 18th day of September 2026', so the timeline entry 2026-09-18 in_force and status in_force are correct. kind executive_order is correct. The issuer is primary. Para 2: GovOps 'shall complete the requirements of subdivision (a) of Section 11549.82 of the Government Code and begin taking the actions required by subdivision (b) of that Section' no later than 1 December 2027. The summary and key_obligations[1] match. Para 3: GovOps 'in consultation with the Governor's Office of Emergency Services' shall by 16 November 2026 'submit to my office recommendations, developed in consultation with national experts, addressing the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments to existing state laws regarding AI safety and security, including at least' items a to d. The deadline and topic framing match. The no-enforceable-rights clause matches. No duplicate in content/instruments (grep for N-9-26, kill switch, 8898.1 found nothing). PROBLEMS: (1) Para 1 of the order reads: 'No later than May 1, 2027, the Government Operations Agency shall complete the requirements of Section 8898.1 of the Government Code and develop application requirements, procedures, and criteria for independent verification organizations and publicly post them, as required by law.' The order joins two actions with 'and'. It does not say that posting application criteria is what Section 8898.1 requires. The summary ('complete the requirements of Gov. Code 8898.1, including posting application requirements and criteria') and key_obligations[0] ('complete Gov. Code 8898.1 requirements (verification organization application criteria)') both describe the content of 8898.1 in a way the cited source does not. I tried to check 8898.1 and 11549.82 directly: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov returned 403, and a web search found no copy of either section. The characterisation is unverified, and the protocol does not allow stating it. (2) key_obligations[2] narrows item (b) to 'independent verification of safety frameworks'. The order covers 'the safety frameworks, transparency reports, and risk assessments that frontier AI companies are required to file'. It also leaves out that the list is a minimum ('at least') and who submits (GovOps in consultation with Cal OES). The summary's 'commissions recommendations' also does not say who submits or to whom. Out of scope but noted: the paired item us-ca-eo-n-9-26-frontier-ai-oversight uses 'the independent verification organization requirements of Government Code section 8898.1', which is a milder form of the same unverified characterisation.
